section: Articles 20, 21, 21A and 22 - protection in conviction, life and liberty, education, preventive detention

accepted.s: In the context of the Supreme Court decision in Vihaan Kumar v. State of Haryana, reported on 14 August 2026, which of the following was emphasised?
o: The grounds of arrest must be meaningfully communicated to every arrestee
The right to education is available only to citizens
Preventive detention can be ordered only after conviction
An Advisory Board must review every arrest within 24 hours
accepted.x: Vihaan Kumar v. State of Haryana emphasised that the grounds of arrest must be meaningfully communicated to every arrestee.
accepted.tq: Directly identify the precise legal requirement associated with a recent case.

accepted.s: Which High Court criticised routine detentions in the Chander Pal Singh case?
o: Madhya Pradesh High Court
Delhi High Court
Punjab and Haryana High Court
Allahabad High Court
accepted.x: The Allahabad High Court criticised routine detentions in the Chander Pal Singh case.
accepted.tq: Use the court-case association rather than confusing similar constitutional forums.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding preventive detention in India:
1. NCRB data indicate more than 1.2 lakh preventive detentions in a year.
2. About half of these detentions have reportedly been quashed by High Courts.
3. The reported data show that preventive detention is confined to only a few dozen cases annually.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: NCRB data indicate more than 1.2 lakh preventive detentions annually, with about half reportedly quashed by High Courts. Statement 3 is false because the number is over 1.2 lakh, not a few dozen.
accepted.tq: Find the exaggerated numerical reversal and retain the two statements carrying the reported figures.

accepted.s: Which case is associated with shaping the right to education in the context of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Vihaan Kumar v. State of Haryana
K.A. Najeeb v. Union of India
Harish Rana v. Union of India
Unnikrishnan v. State of Andhra Pradesh
accepted.x: Unnikrishnan v. State of Andhra Pradesh, decided in 1993, played an important role in shaping the right to education.
accepted.tq: Match the constitutional theme with the correct case name and State connection.

accepted.s: The criticism concerning the Forty-Fourth Amendment in the context of preventive detention is that a relevant clause remains—
o: applicable only during a financial emergency
repealed without legislative replacement
limited exclusively to foreign nationals
unnotified and therefore not brought into operation
accepted.x: The criticism is that the relevant Forty-Fourth Amendment clause has remained unnotified and has not been brought into operation.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an unnotified constitutional provision from a repealed or inapplicable one.

accepted.s: Which of the following is a criticism associated with the operation of preventive detention laws?
o: Preventive detention requires a prior final conviction in every case
Preventive detention applies only to civil disputes
The expression “public order” may be used vaguely
Advisory Boards are constitutionally prohibited from reviewing detention
accepted.x: The vague use of the expression “public order” is a recognised criticism in debates concerning preventive detention.
accepted.tq: Select the legally relevant criticism and reject options that reverse the nature of preventive detention.

accepted.s: With reference to bail in cases under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, the Supreme Court has observed that delay alone is—
o: an automatic ground for acquittal
a constitutional bar on prosecution
not a trump card for granting bail
sufficient to invalidate the detention order
accepted.x: The Supreme Court observed on 6 January 2026 that delay alone is not a “trump card” for bail in UAPA cases.
accepted.tq: Test the exact legal qualification instead of treating delay as an automatic remedy.

accepted.s: A letter concerning the cases of Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam, citing the precedent of K.A. Najeeb, was addressed to—
o: The Attorney General of India
The Union Home Secretary
Chief Justice Surya Kant
The Chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission
accepted.x: The letter was addressed to Chief Justice Surya Kant and cited the K.A. Najeeb precedent in relation to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam. It was reported on 15 August 2026.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct constitutional authority from a cluster of closely related legal actors.

accepted.s: Harish Rana, who had remained in a persistent vegetative state for 13 years, became the subject of proceedings concerning—
o: withdrawal of life support before the Supreme Court
enforcement of the right to education
communication of grounds of arrest
appointment to an Advisory Board for preventive detention
accepted.x: In the Harish Rana matter, his parents sought withdrawal of life support before the Supreme Court after he had remained in a persistent vegetative state for 13 years.
accepted.tq: Apply the factual setting to identify the precise constitutional and medical-legal issue.

accepted.s: The demand to notify the relevant Forty-Fourth Amendment provision concerning preventive detention relates to limiting detention without Advisory Board confirmation to—
o: six months
three months
one month
two months
accepted.x: The demand concerns notification of the Forty-Fourth Amendment provision prescribing a two-month limit in the relevant preventive-detention context.
accepted.tq: Focus on the exact statutory time limit and distinguish it from familiar three- and six-month periods.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding constitutional approaches to personal liberty:
1. “Procedure established by law” is associated with Japan.
2. “Due process” is associated with the United States of America.
3. The two expressions are identified with the same constitutional system.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: “Procedure established by law” is associated with Japan, while “due process” is associated with the United States. Statement 3 is false because the expressions are associated with different constitutional systems.
accepted.tq: Separate the two confusable constitutional expressions by their country of association.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with the principal subject of the indicated constitutional Article?
o: Article 20 — protection in respect of conviction for offences
Article 21 — preventive detention and safeguards against arrest
Article 21A — protection against ex post facto criminal laws
Article 22 — compulsory education for children aged six to fourteen years
accepted.x: Article 20 provides protection in respect of conviction for offences. Article 21 concerns life and personal liberty, Article 21A concerns education, and Article 22 deals with protection against arrest and detention, including preventive detention safeguards.
accepted.tq: Use article–subject matching and eliminate options formed by swapping neighbouring Fundamental Rights.
